Definition: from G2170; to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal:--(give) thank(-ful, -s).
BiblicalUsage: Eucharistéō means to give thanks — to express gratitude to God, actively and out loud. Jesus gives thanks before He breaks the bread; Paul gives thanks for every church he writes to; and we are told to give thanks in everything. It is the word for gratitude turned into speech.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe eucharistéō is a discipline, not a feeling: thanks given, not merely felt, is what changes a heart. I hold that giving thanks in everything is the way to see God's hand in everything.
RelatedEvents: The Last Supper; The Feeding of the Four Thousand
